message.content:
You are a citation DOI resolver. For each of the following 5 real papers (taken verbatim from a thesis bibliography), confirm the DOI via web search (CrossRef/PubMed/publisher). Then, where easily found in an abstract or open-access text, capture ONE short VERBATIM quote of the specific numeric range/value the paper reports (these are mechanical modulus / thickness values). NEVER fabricate a quote — if you cannot fetch one, set quote=null and access="metadata_only". Resolve a real DOI; if none can be confirmed, set doi=null and note it.

Use WebSearch and WebFetch tools. To load them, first call ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch".

Papers:

11. key=holzapfel2005 — Holzapfel GA, Sommer G, Gasser CT, Regitnig P, "Determination of layer-specific mechanical properties of human coronary arteries with nonatherosclerotic intimal thickening and related constitutive modeling," Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol 2005;289(5):H2048-H2058. Need: a quote about vessel-wall stiffness/modulus values.

12. key=loree1994static — Loree HM, Grodzinsky AJ, Park SY, Gibson LJ, Lee RT, "Static circumferential tangential modulus of human atherosclerotic tissue," J Biomech 1994;27(2):195-204. Need: a quote about fibrous-cap / cellular / hypocellular / calcified tangential modulus values (kPa).

13. key=loree1994lipid — Loree HM, Tobias BJ, Gibson LJ, Kamm RD, Small DM, Lee RT, "Mechanical properties of model atherosclerotic lesion lipid pools," Arterioscler Thromb 1994;14(2):230-234. Need: a quote about lipid-pool / lipid-core modulus values.

14. key=ebenstein2009 — Ebenstein DM, Coughlin D, Chapman J, Li C, Pruitt LA, "Nanomechanical properties of calcification, fibrous tissue, and hematoma from atherosclerotic plaques," J Biomed Mater Res A 2009;91(4):1028-1037. Need: a quote about calcification modulus (GPa/MPa) values.

15. key=yonetsu2011 — Yonetsu T, Kakuta T, Lee T, et al., "In vivo critical fibrous cap thickness for rupture-prone coronary plaques assessed by optical coherence tomography," Eur Heart J 2011;32(10):1251-1259. Need: a quote about the critical/cutoff fibrous cap thickness (e.g. ~80 um cutoff, or 100 um).

Return a structured result for EACH paper: key | confirmed DOI (or null) | PMID if found | confirmed? (yes/no) | verbatim quote (or null) | access (full_text/abstract_only/metadata_only) | source URL you used. Be concise. Do NOT write any files.

**Journal and Volume:**

The article appeared in American Journal of Physiology-Heart and Circulatory Physiology, Volume 289(5), pages 2048-2058 (2005).

**Study Overview:**

The study examined 13 nonstenotic human left anterior descending coronary arteries from subjects with a mean age of 71.5 ± 7.3 years. Preconditioned prepared strips (n = 78) from individual layers were subjected to cyclic quasi-static uniaxial tension tests in axial and circumferential directions.

**Key Finding:**

The study showed the need to model nonstenotic human coronary arteries with nonatherosclerotic intimal thickening as a composite structure composed of three solid mechanically relevant layers with different mechanical properties.

# Abstract Text

The abstractText field states:

"Clinical events such as heart attack and stroke can be caused by the rupture of atherosclerotic plaques in artery walls. Computational modeling is often used to better understand atherosclerotic disease progression to identify \"vulnerable\" plaques (i.e., those likely to rupture) and to tailor treatments according to tissue composition. However, because of the heterogeneity of plaque tissue, there are limited data available on the material properties of individual plaque constituents. The goal of this study was to use nanoindentation to measure the mechanical properties of blood clots, fibrous tissue, partially calcified fibrous tissue, and bulk calcifications from human atherosclerotic plaque tissue. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy was used to quantify the amount of mineral and lipid in each tissue region tested. The results demonstrate that the stiffness of plaque tissue increases with increasing mineral content. In addition, by providing the first experimental data on atherosclerotic calcifications, these data show that some of the estimated modulus values commonly used in computational models greatly underestimate the stiffness of the fully calcified tissue."

## Calcification Modulus Values

No specific modulus values in GPa or MPa are reported in the abstract. The text notes that "estimated modulus values commonly used in computational models greatly underestimate the stiffness of the fully calcified tissue," but does not provide numerical measurements.
